svg.title: Base Case: $1,010,000 Gross to $191,900 Owner Profit
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-profit-bridge; chart type: waterfall; title: Base Case: $1,010,000 Gross to $191,900 Owner Profit; subtitle: Six signed bars end at 19.0% gross margin and 47.5% retained margin.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Formula v2.0 fixes gross billings, retained_share=0.4, and owner profit; the expense split below is an illustrative allocation that reconciles exactly. Gross billings are not net-presented operator revenue. Normalize fee-net exchange remittances back to gross once, then deduct the sell fee once. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to actual contracts before choosing financial-statement presentation; the scorecard uses 40% retained revenue. Owner profit is after modeled operating costs and funding expense, before owner-specific income taxes.; caption: $1,010,000 - $606,000 - $80,800 - $40,400 - $20,200 - $70,700 = $191,900. Retained revenue is $404,000; $191,900 / $404,000 = 47.5%. Conservative: $220,000 gross, $88,000 retained, $26,400 profit, 12% gross margin, 30% retained margin, 1 FT + 2 C. Base: $1,010,000 gross, $404,000 retained, $191,900 profit, 19.0% gross margin, 47.5% retained margin, 1 FT + 2 C. Scaled: $1,800,000 gross, $720,000 retained, $468,000 profit, 26% gross margin, 65% retained margin, 2 FT + 3 C. The sixth bar ends at profit; do not append profit as another additive bar.; stages: label: Gross customer billings; value: +$1,010,000 annual gross; numeric value: 1010000.0; detail: Aggregate secondary ticket sales, suite-seat sales, and VIP package billings before the modeled acquisition and selling deductions. Exclude taxes collected for authorities and refundable customer deposits awaiting performance.; label: Ticket and suite acquisition; value: -$606,000; $404,000 retained; numeric value: -606000.0; detail: Deduct 60% of gross for face-value inventory and contracted ticket, suite, and package acquisition. The resulting 40% retained spread is $404,000, not the owner's profit.; label: Exchange and collection fees; value: -$80,800; $323,200 remaining; numeric value: -80800.0; detail: Model blended exchange sell fees and direct collection charges at 8% of gross. Match fee schedules to each rail; do not apply an exchange fee again to an already fee-net remittance.; label: Unsold inventory and markdown loss; value: -$40,400; $282,800 remaining; numeric value: -40400.0; detail: Charge 4% of gross for incremental unsold inventory write-offs and markdown variance against the acquisition baseline. Do not deduct a realized markdown twice when actual gross billings already include its price effect.; label: Event disruption loss provision; value: -$20,200; $262,600 remaining; numeric value: -20200.0; detail: Charge 2% of gross for expected postponement, cancellation, refund, and clawback losses net of supportable supplier recoveries. Maintain a separate cash liquidity reserve; moving cash into that reserve is not another expense.; label: Operating and funding expense; value: -$70,700; $191,900 owner profit; numeric value: -70700.0; detail: Allocate $64,700 to contractor compensation, POS services, administration, and other operating costs, plus $6,000 to inventory and delayed-payout funding expense. Combined monthly cost averages $5,891.67. Payout delay itself changes cash timing; its funding cost reduces profit.

text.title: Base Case: $1,010,000 Gross to $191,900 Owner Profit
text.tspan: Base Case: $1,010,000 Gross to $191,900 Owner Profit

rect.title: label: Gross customer billings; value: +$1,010,000 annual gross; numeric value: 1010000.0; detail: Aggregate secondary ticket sales, suite-seat sales, and VIP package billings before the modeled acquisition and selling deductions. Exclude taxes collected for authorities and refundable customer deposits awaiting performance.

label: Ticket and suite acquisition; value: -$606,000; $404,000 retained; numeric value: -606000.0; detail: Deduct 60% of gross for face-value inventory and contracted ticket, suite, and package acquisition. The resulting 40% retained spread is $404,000, not the owner's profit.

label: Exchange and collection fees; value: -$80,800; $323,200 remaining; numeric value: -80800.0; detail: Model blended exchange sell fees and direct collection charges at 8% of gross. Match fee schedules to each rail; do not apply an exchange fee again to an already fee-net remittance.

label: Unsold inventory and markdown loss; value: -$40,400; $282,800 remaining; numeric value: -40400.0; detail: Charge 4% of gross for incremental unsold inventory write-offs and markdown variance against the acquisition baseline. Do not deduct a realized markdown twice when actual gross billings already include its price effect.

label: Event disruption loss provision; value: -$20,200; $262,600 remaining; numeric value: -20200.0; detail: Charge 2% of gross for expected postponement, cancellation, refund, and clawback losses net of supportable supplier recoveries. Maintain a separate cash liquidity reserve; moving cash into that reserve is not another expense.

label: Operating and funding expense; value: -$70,700; $191,900 owner profit; numeric value: -70700.0; detail: Allocate $64,700 to contractor compensation, POS services, administration, and other operating costs, plus $6,000 to inventory and delayed-payout funding expense. Combined monthly cost averages $5,891.67. Payout delay itself changes cash timing; its funding cost reduces profit.

text.title: Assumptions: Formula v2.0 fixes gross billings, retained_share=0.4, and owner profit; the expense split below is an illustrative allocation that reconciles exactly. Gross billings are not net-presented operator revenue. Normalize fee-net exchange remittances back to gross once, then deduct the sell fee once. Apply ASC 606 principal-versus-agent analysis to actual contracts before choosing financial-statement presentation; the scorecard uses 40% retained revenue. Owner profit is after modeled operating costs and funding expense, before owner-specific income taxes.
